items.t: Millicom Stock Revenue Beat Raises Margin Questions After Q3 Earnings
sum: Millicom International Cellular reported Q3 2026 sales of US$2,276 million and net income of US$98 million, with earnings per share of US$0.58 from continuing operations, while reaffirming full year equity free cash flow guidance of around US$1.1 billion and a leverage goal below 2.5x.

Management highlighted progress on its Double E and more for more plans, including significant postpaid migration from the prepaid base and stronger convergence. This helped deliver US$2.28 billion in quarterly revenue that exceeded some analyst expectations, even as earnings per share fell short of consensus forecasts.
The next area of focus will be how Millicom’s revenue outperformance, alongside an earnings miss, may reshape the broader investment narrative.

To own Millicom International Cellular, you need to buy into a Latin American telecom story built on postpaid upgrades, convergence and disciplined cash generation. The latest quarter still leans into that idea. Service revenue was solid, equity free cash flow guidance of about US$1.1b was reaffirmed and the leverage goal below 2.5x stayed intact.

The short term swing factor is whether earnings pressure eases while debt keeps trending lower. Q3 net income and EPS were weaker than a year ago, so any delay in margin recovery or higher interest costs remains the biggest operational risk. On this front, the earnings miss looks important, not noise.

The most relevant update alongside the earnings print is management’s confirmation that Millicom International Cellular is on track for roughly US$1.1b in equity free cash flow in 2026 while targeting leverage below 2.5x. For a business carrying about US$8.1b of net debt, that cash profile sits at the center of the thesis.

That same announcement underlined execution on the Double E and more for more plans, with 73% of postpaid sales coming from the prepaid base and strong take up of convergent offers. For you, the key question is whether this operational mix shift offsets margin pressure and refinancing risk quickly enough to keep that cash flow target credible.

items.t: Buy, Sell, or Hold? Tuesday's Top Upgrades and Downgrades: AON, Bloom Energy, Chevron, Cloudflare, Marvell Technologies, Lumentum Holdings, Merck & Co., Roku, X-Energy, and More
sum: Tech stocks keep beating estimates and then selling off anyway, Apple just joined the club, and Wall Street analysts are busy reshuffling their ratings on everything from nuclear energy plays to insurance giants. Here is who got upgraded, downgraded, and…

Futures are trading mixed early Tuesday, with the Dow Futures down 300 points after yet another tech titan posted outstanding numbers that beat Wall Street estimates, then, like clockwork, sold off in the aftermarket. This time, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL | AAPL Price Prediction) was the victim; while it was torpedoed after the results were posted, it was still down less than some other mega-cap technology stocks that reported over the last 10 days. iPhone sales were outstanding as demand for the iPhone 18 surged, while service revenue hit an all-time high of $31.57 billion. Reasons for the post-earnings sell-off ranged from the company missing revenue estimates for China to rising costs for memory chips, which are starting to pressure gross margins, which the company lowered for the December quarter. The bottom line is the tech sell-off and investor rotation likely still have a way to go.

After a solid start to the trading week, stocks rolled over after the noon hour, and the same reasons stayed front and center. Massive AI spending and worries about big tech stocks’ lack of free cash flow, which in the past had never been an issue, and concerns over the potential for the Democrats to regain the House of Representatives are all contributing to a quiet market sell-off, and with the October jobs report this Friday and the inflation reports next week all still on the burner, those data points will have the ability to move the market.

Three of the four major indices closed lower Monday, with only the Dow Jones Industrials closing higher at 51,938, up 0.41%, while the Nasdaq was the big loser Monday, closing at 25,164, down 1.07%. The S&P 500 ended the session at 7,541, down 0.51%, and the small-cap Russell 2000 closed at 2,805, down 0.21%.

Desktop stock: Claro NXT completes 72.83% acquisition
sum: Claro NXT, a subsidiary of América Móvil, completed the acquisition of a controlling stake in Desktop on October 1, 2026. In its Form 6-K, América Móvil said its Brazilian subsidiary acquired 72.83% of Desktop's capital stock.

The deal transfers control of the Brazilian telecommunications provider to Claro NXT. Telecompaper reported that Claro NXT intends to submit a request to Brazil's securities regulator for a unified tender offer for the remaining shares.

The proposed process is also intended to facilitate a change in Desktop's issuer registration from Category A to Category B. For minority shareholders, the next key developments are the tender-offer terms and the regulatory process that follows the change of control.

Desktop is a Brazilian telecommunications provider focused on internet and connectivity services. Its operations are now being integrated into Claro NXT's fixed broadband platform, giving América Móvil a larger regional infrastructure and customer base in Brazil. The ownership change places Desktop within the expansion of Claro's fixed-network business rather than leaving it as an independent listed operator.
Brazil's broader equity market can be followed through the Bovespa index.

For investors, the tender offer and any subsequent changes to Desktop's listing status are more immediate issues than operating results. The final terms and regulatory filings will determine the options available to remaining shareholders.

items.t: Earnings call transcript: América Móvil tops revenue in Q3 2026 as stock rises
America Movil SAB de CV Stock (AMX) Moved Up by 5.46% on Oct 21: A Full Analysis
sum: America Movil SAB de CV (AMX) moved up by 5.46%. The Telecommunications Services sector is up by 3.59%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: SpaceX (SPCX) up 6.42%; AT&T Inc (T) down 6.23%; Verizon Communications Inc (VZ) down 2.37%.

América Móvil registered a strong upward rally during today's trading session, driven primarily by investor enthusiasm following the release of its third-quarter financial results. The Latin American telecommunications giant delivered top-line revenue growth that surpassed consensus Wall Street expectations, bolstered by resilient consumer demand across its core geographic segments. A sharp expansion in postpaid mobile subscribers across key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and Colombia served as a primary growth driver, reinforcing the company's leading market share and pricing power across the region.

Beyond top-line momentum, operational efficiency and profitability metrics provided strong support for the stock's positive price action. EBITDA grew at a faster pace than overall service revenue, demonstrating improved margin performance and tight cost discipline across network operations. Free cash flow generation experienced significant year-over-year acceleration, providing management with amplified flexibility to fully fund cash flows while maintaining active share buyback programs and dividend distributions. Furthermore, continued progress in balance sheet leverage reduction strengthened institutional confidence in the firm's long-term capital structure.

Market sentiment was further bolstered during the management conference call, where executives highlighted stable demand trends, competitive advantages in 5G deployment, and disciplined capital allocation. Analysts responded favorably to the company's ongoing strategic transition toward enhanced capital return yields following recent tactical consolidation in regional markets. The combination of better-than-expected revenue, expanding operating margins, robust cash generation, and reassuring forward guidance prompted widespread institutional buying, pushing the stock sharply higher with elevated trading activity.

Amer Movil (AMX) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
sum: Amer Movil (AMX) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.47 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.46 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.4 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.17%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this telecommunications company would post earnings of $0.52 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.47, delivering a surprise of -9.62%.
Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates just once.

Amer Movil, which belongs to the Zacks Wireless Non-US industry, posted revenues of $14.53 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.16%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $12.51 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.
The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.
Amer Movil shares have added about 10.5% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.4%.
While Amer Movil has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

items.t: Telefonica Brasil SA Stock (VIV) Moved Up by 10.92% on Oct 5: What Investors Need To Know
sum: Telefonica Brasil SA (VIV) moved up by 10.92%. The Telecommunications Services sector is up by 4.70%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: SpaceX (SPCX) up 6.62%; Verizon Communications Inc (VZ) down 0.53%; AT&T Inc (T) down 0.86%.

Telefônica Brasil S.A. surged sharply during trading, driven by a convergence of technical momentum, renewed institutional interest, and favorable macroeconomic dynamics surrounding Latin American telecommunications assets. Following a period of price consolidation, the stock reached key technical support levels that attracted disciplined institutional buyers and momentum-driven quantitative strategies. The strong pre-market buying pressure triggered short-covering activity and heightened volume participation, accelerating the upward momentum throughout the session.

Fundamentally, investor sentiment remains anchored by the company's leadership position in the Brazilian telecommunications sector through its dominant Vivo brand. Telefônica Brasil continues to generate steady cash flows through its expansion in high-margin fiber-to-the-home connections and premium postpaid mobile subscriptions. Management's ongoing commitment to shareholder remuneration—supported by robust dividend payouts, interest on capital, and ongoing share buyback or capital reduction initiatives—enhances its overall investment thesis for income-oriented portfolios.

From a broader market perspective, positive sentiment across emerging market equities and underlying currency stability provided additional support for the American Depositary Shares. As expectations around domestic monetary policy and local interest rate pressures begin to stabilize, capital is increasingly rotating back into defensive, cash-generative telecom operators with solid balance sheets. Today's upward movement reflects a major bullish re-rating as market participants capitalize on the stock's operational execution and elevated yield potential.

items.t: SBA goes all-in on Central America with 600 towers planned for 2026
sum: SBA Communications plans to build about 600 towers in 2026, most of them in Central America, as the US tower operator expands its international footprint to serve Millicom and other regional carriers.

International builds accelerated in the second quarter, with 99 new towers completed compared to 75 in the first quarter, and the company expects the pace to increase in each successive quarter this year.

"In the second quarter, we saw increased new tower construction as we ramped up efforts in Central America building sites for Millicom and others," CEO Brendan Cavanagh said during the earnings results release.

SBA owned 10,948 sites in the region at the end of the second quarter, up from 10,905 in the first quarter, while its global portfolio grew to 46,390 sites from 46,358. South America, by contrast, edged down slightly to 14,326 sites from 14,347 over the same period.

The customer base behind SBA's international revenue also shifted. Millicom's Tigo share of international site leasing revenue jumped to 19.6% in the second quarter from 6.7% a year earlier, while Telefónica's share fell to 18.7% from 21.8%. América Móvil eased to 19.4% from 19.8%, and TIM slipped to 12.2% from 14.0%.

Asked on the earnings call about tower rents in Latin America, Cavanagh said the dynamic there is not fundamentally different from SBA's other markets, since all customers are looking for ways to control costs, including their rents.

"It's really a matter of making sure that what we're delivering to them is of greater value than the costs that they're incurring in order to be there," he said, adding that high-quality locations and responsive service and support help the company retain tenants. Cases where a customer drops a site because it is no longer needed or a cheaper alternative exists do happen, he said, but are "more the exception than the rule."
